dataset.name: Online Retail II
dataset.citation: Chen, D. (2019). Online Retail II. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D
dataset.population: one UK-registered, non-store online retailer selling giftware, mostly to wholesale buyers, 2009-12-01 to 2011-12-09

sibling_lab.its_question: how many units of this product will we sell next week?
sibling_lab.our_question: which products should we show this shopper?

split.why_not_random: A random split puts December's baskets in training and September's in test. No one can ask that question in production, and the model has seen the future it is graded on.

standard.name: Standard next-purchase
standard.ground_truth: every product the customer bought in the test window, repeats included
standard.candidates: the whole catalog; products the customer already owns are NOT masked
standard.question: did we predict what this customer bought next?

discovery.name: Discovery
discovery.ground_truth: only products the customer had NEVER bought before the cut
discovery.candidates: the catalog minus everything in the customer's training history
discovery.question: did we predict something this customer would not otherwise have found?

incoherent-middle.name: The incoherent middle
incoherent-middle.ground_truth: every product bought in the test window, repeats included
incoherent-middle.candidates: the catalog minus the customer's history - so 38.4% of the truth is unreachable
incoherent-middle.question: none that is answerable - this is the protocol bug to recognize

reorder_zero_score_diagnosis.explanation: With every already-bought product masked, this model scores zero everywhere. Its ten slots are the first ten products in index order, which is a tie-break, not a ranking - and a tie-break that lands in the least-bought tail of the catalog.

leaderboards.rule: Coverage and novelty are printed beside every accuracy number, always. Neither leaderboard is optional.

incremental_revenue.boundary: an offline ranking score is not evidence of revenue; the model ranks within a merchandiser's rules and never decides what a shopper needs

cold_start.warning: The cold-registered share and the guest share are different populations measured against different denominators. They must never be added together or used interchangeably.

policy.eligibility: products the customer has NEVER purchased in the training window
policy.fallback_rule: recent revenue, last 28 days of the training window

reload_check.selection: the discovery-protocol population sorted by customer id, first 200

exposure_loop.assumption_note: 5% of shown slots convert. This is a classroom assumption chosen to make the mechanism visible in ten rounds. It is NOT measured from this data and must be captioned as an assumption anywhere it appears.

leave_one_out.design: Targets fixed at one product per customer. Only the training data changes, so the gap is the leak.
